title: Martin Romualdez appeals 90-day suspension, says plunder allegations unclear
summary: Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has appealed the 90-day suspension imposed by the Sandiganbayan, saying it is premature amid the prosecution"s unclear P7.4 billion plunder charge.

blocks.text: Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has appealed the 90-day suspension imposed by the Sandiganbayan, saying it is premature amid the prosecution’s unclear P7.4 billion plunder charge.

In his motion for reconsideration, Romualdez said the Sandiganbayan did not rule on his argument that the prosecution did not identify a main plunderer, even if a 2016 Supreme Court ruling on the Arroyo v. People case requires that such should be identified when a case is filed against several individuals.

“With due respect, the [criminal] Information charges accused Romualdez and Co together with receiving the monies “by reason or on account of the respective public offices and positions of Romualdez and Co,” and with “taking undue advantage, on several occasions, of their respective official positions, authorities, relationships, connections, or influence to unjustly enrich themselves.” It does not state which of the two is the main plunderer, either does it state how much of the aggregate of P7.4 billion each of them supposedly amassed,” the former House speaker said in his appeal.

“The Questioned Resolution [imposing a suspension order] reads the Information as alleging that accused Romualdez amassed the ill-gotten wealth. The Information does not allege that accused Romualdez, as distinguished from Co, amassed it. It alleges only that Romualdez and Co enriched “themselves.” This, too, must be resolved before the Information may serve as the basis for preventive suspension,” he added.

Romualdez’s co-accused in the P7.4 billion plunder case include former House appropriations chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.

“Accused Romualdez is not identified as having personally received any sum on any of the 15 occasions alleged. Neither does the [criminal information distinguish supposed receipts by an approximate date, amount, or identified transaction. A bare statement of 15 occasions, an aggregate amount, and delivery locations, do not sufficiently identify the component criminal transactions comprising the alleged series,” the lawmaker said.

Romualdez said that while the issue on whether he committed the alleged acts is a matter for trial, whether those acts have been sufficiently alleged is another question that needs to be resolved first.
“The latter must be resolved before the [criminal] information may serve as the basis for preventive suspension,” he said. —AOL, GMA News
